headline: Bidirectional sensing-behavior information flow underlies navigation across organisms
label: Information Flow In Navigation
summary: Transfer-entropy frameworks now quantify bidirectional sensing-behavior information flow in navigation across organisms and agents.
synthesis: The dominant thread is navigation treated as a closed sensing-behavior loop, quantified by bidirectional transfer entropy. Two preprints formalize this information flow: one applies the framework to bacterial, worm, and fly trajectories and reinforcement learning agents, while the other links navigation performance to bidirectional transfer entropy between sensing and actuation, with E. coli simulations as confirmation. The novelty lies in a quantitative, information-theoretic account spanning organisms. The published place-cell study operates at a different level, showing that a neuromodulated model forms cognitive maps online within a single simulated trial during reward-driven navigation in novel environments. The head-direction spiking model addresses uncertainty through fluctuations rather than information flow. The items do not test whether these share a mechanism, so a common mechanistic basis remains an open question.
